grades.quote: xv6 uses locks around accesses to shared data.
grades.reason: Identifies locks as shared-data synchronization, but does not explain the limits of disabling local interrupts.

grades.quote: This doesn’t work on a multi-core machine, since each CPU executes a different process.
grades.reason: Provides the supporting fact that CPUs execute different processes, but does not explain why local interrupt disabling leaves other CPUs unaffected.

grades.quote: Xv6 is more conservative: when a CPU acquires any lock, xv6 always disables interrupts on that CPU. Interrupts may still occur on other CPUs, so an interrupt’s acquire can wait for a thread to release a spinlock; just not on the same CPU.
grades.reason: Directly explains that disabling interrupts affects only that CPU; other CPUs remain active, requiring a spinlock for shared-data synchronization.
Discusses memory protection and Itanium protection keys, not interrupt disabling or multiprocessor synchronization.
